title: From Proposal to Design: Decomposition, Contracts, Modules
summary: Split user stories into features and features into functions (the verb test), write each function's contract (name, arguments, return value, failure) in its docstring, and divide responsibilities among four modules: main, logic, storage and report. Run the finished study_logger and refactor_lab, which splits a one-function expense tracker.

study_logger.summary: The finished study-time logger. main.py only asks, calls and shows; the rules live in logic.py (no I/O), files in storage.py, and the text for the screen in report.py. test_logic.py is a check file that writes the proposal's acceptance criteria as asserts.
study_logger.notes: Step 2 adds one row (2026-10-26,python,60) to data/study.csv. To return to the original state, reload the page. The test_logic.py in this folder is not unittest but a script listing asserts, so run it with python3 test_logic.py.
steps: The same as the project-folder layout on the slide: code files at the top level, data in data/. The CSV has the header date,course,minutes and 2 sample rows.

The three input lines (date, course, minutes) were fed in with printf. You can also run python3 main.py yourself and type them. Even with mixed case and a space as in 'Python ', make_record's strip().lower() turns it into python, so it is added to the same course: python 150 min, stats 45 min. report.py sorts the output from the largest total down.

logic only raises ValueError; main decides the sentence the user sees (Not saved: ...). For -30 it is our own message; for abc it is the invalid literal message from int(). Neither is saved, so the file stays at the header plus 3 rows, 4 lines.
This checks only the logic functions, with no keyboard and no files. It takes less than a second and you can rerun it after every change. All checks passed. means the acceptance criteria pass.
The docstring is the contract. Its first line says what is returned: Return text as a positive whole number of minutes.

The example from the slide 'Importing your own files'. logic.py and report.py in the same folder are imported by module name. One record is a dict with fixed keys ({'date': ..., 'course': 'stats', 'minutes': 45}, minutes is an int), all records are a list of dicts, and the totals are a dict from course to minutes.
csv.DictReader uses the header as keys, but every value is a str. '90' + '45' becomes 9045, not 135. That is why storage.load_records converts with int() once, right after reading.

Import trap 1: if you name a file after a standard-library module, your own file hides the real module. /tmp/trap/csv.py is loaded and has no DictReader (False). If this happens in a project, you get AttributeError: module 'csv' has no attribute 'DictReader'. Rename the file and delete __pycache__ to fix it.

refactor_lab.summary: Practice 2: read all_in_one(), an expense tracker that crams input, checking, totaling and output into one function, and move its rules into three I/O-free functions: parse_amount, category_totals and format_report. Each docstring is the contract; keep fixing until all six checks are PASS.
refactor_lab.notes: There is no solution file for this lab. Hint: ' food ' and 'Food' are the same category, so apply strip() and lower() before adding. parse_amount has the same kind of contract as logic.parse_minutes in study_logger.
steps: In the starting state the TODO functions return only placeholder values (0, {}, []), so most checks FAIL. Compare got and expected on each FAIL line to see what to fix. category_totals([]) happens to PASS because the placeholder empty dict is the right answer.

Run the original one-piece function with some input. -200 is Skipped, and ' food ' and 'Food' are combined as the same food, giving bus: 1500 won, food: 12500 won. This is the same result as the expected value of the format_report check. Having to type the input every time you want to test this totaling rule is exactly why decomposition is needed.

The places to complete are TODO 1–3. Do not use input() or print() inside the three functions. Edit with nano refactor_lab.py, then run python3 refactor_lab.py again and check that six PASS lines appear.
